newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa earnings firm in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa earnings firm in fourth quarter.

text.p: Aluminum Co of America on Wednesday reported fourth quarter earnings of $152.9 million, or $0.88 per share, before a charge of $16.8 million, or $0.10 per share, for impairments.
Fourth quarter 1995 net income was $150.9 million, or 85 cents per share. The First Call consensus estimate for the latest quarter was $0.86.

Fourth quarter 1996 earnings included after-tax gains of $8 million, or $0.05 per share, as a result of marking to market (valuing at market instead of contract prices) certain aluminum commodity contracts, Alcoa said.

Of these gains, $3.3 million, or $0.02 per share, is attributable to fabricated product sales contracts that were delivered during the fourth quarter and $4.7 million, or $0.03 cents per share, is related to fabricated product sales contracts that will be shipped in future quarters.

For all of 1996, Alcoa earned $637.2 million, or $3.65 per share, before a charge of $122.3 million, or $0.70 per share, for layoff provisions and impairments. For the year 1995, net income was $790.5 million, or $4.43 per share.
Results for 1996 also include losses of $57.1 million, or $0.33 cents per share, for marking to market certain aluminum commodity contracts during the year.

For 1996, higher alumina prices, improved performance and increased sales of non-aluminum products partially offset the impact of aluminum price declines, higher raw materials costs and marking to market adjustments compared with 1995.

Aided by Alcoa's acquired operations in Italy, the company said shipments of aluminum products during the 1996 fourth quarter amounted to 747,000 metric tonnes compared with 646,000 tonnnes in the year ago quarter. For all of 1996, shipments were 2,841,000 tonnes compared with 2,582,000 tonnes in 1995.
